topic: Hugh has been asked by the widow to give the eulogy on Friday for Clive Morgan, who farmed next door to him for forty years and was, by common agreement in town, a difficult, mean-spirited man who once moved a boundary fence by six feet. Hugh has just said to the table: 'I don't know what I'm meant to say about him.'

T.speaker: Rhi
T.line: Six feet, Hugh. You could start with the six feet.

T.speaker: Hugh
T.line: Six and a half, he'd say.

T.speaker: Femi
T.line: Which way, though?

T.speaker: Danny
T.line: Into Hugh's. Improved it, probably.

T.speaker: Sunny
T.line: Hang on, Hugh, is it you can't think of anything nice, or you've got plenty and none of it's fit for a church?

T.speaker: Hugh
T.line: Bit of both. He pulled me out of a ditch once, winter of '83. Sent me a bill for the diesel the Tuesday after.

T.speaker: Jess
T.line: Wait, did you pay it?
T.full: Wait, did you pay it? Because if you paid it, that's a lovely story, but it's about you, Hugh.

T.speaker: Hugh
T.line: Paid it that Friday. Then sent him one back for the gatepost his tractor took out pulling me free.

T.speaker: Femi
T.line: And did he pay yours?

T.speaker: Hugh
T.line: Still waiting.

T.speaker: Danny
T.line: So technically he died
T.full: So technically he died owing you.

T.speaker: Jess
T.line: Owing you a gatepost. Lead with that.

T.speaker: Rhi
T.line: In a church, Jess? Christ.

T.speaker: Femi
T.line: Is the gatepost in the will?

T.speaker: Danny
T.line: Why's everyone looking

T.speaker: Sunny
T.line: You'd bill the widow, bab.

T.speaker: Danny
T.line: No, no, listen, he wasn't mean, Hugh. He was itemised. Every favour, a receipt by Tuesday.

T.speaker: Hugh
T.line: Itemised. I could say that.

T.speaker: Rhi
T.line: Says the man
T.full: Says the man who invoiced back.

T.speaker: Femi
T.line: You're both itemised, then.

T.speaker: Hugh
T.line: Well, we are. That's, that's rather the point, isn't it. Forty years I've kept his tab. Nobody else in that church will know he still owes me a gatepost.

T.speaker: Danny
T.line: Say exactly that. Sunny, no?

T.speaker: Sunny
T.line: Yeah, all right, the gatepost's true, I'll give you that. But she asked you, Hugh
T.full: Yeah, all right, the gatepost's true, I'll give you that. But she asked you, Hugh. She thinks you've got something nicer than a bill.

T.speaker: Jess
T.line: Or she asked you 'cause you're the only one who knew him well enough to hate him properly. Can't prove it, but I'd bet my deposit on it.

T.speaker: Rhi
T.line: Let Sunny finish, for God's sake.

T.speaker: Sunny
T.line: Ta, Rhi. So why you, Hugh?

T.speaker: Hugh
T.line: I asked her that. She said it was his idea
T.full: I asked her that. She said it was his idea, last spring. Probably wanted me stood up there owing him something.

T.speaker: Rhi
T.line: His idea? Oh, the crafty bastard.

T.speaker: Jess
T.line: He's billed you. From the coffin.

T.speaker: Femi
T.line: Hang on, when did he say that?

T.speaker: Hugh
T.line: September, in the hospice. Told her I'd keep it short
T.full: September, in the hospice. Told her I'd keep it short, and I wouldn't charge.

T.speaker: Sunny
T.line: Short? Forty years over the fence and he's ordered it short, like a trim at the barber's.

backchannels.after: like a trim at the barber's

T.speaker: Danny
T.line: No, no, short is a kindness, Sunny. From Clive, ordering it short is practically a hug.

T.speaker: Sunny
T.line: Ar, go on. A small one.

T.speaker: Jess
T.line: Matt's dad's already told us he wants Grease at his. The whole thing, the car bit
T.full: Matt's dad's already told us he wants Grease at his. The whole thing, the car bit and everything. You've got it easy, Hugh.

T.speaker: Femi
T.line: All right, fine, short's a hug, Danny, you can have that one. But the whole of Grease? That's, what, an hour fifty? There'll be the next funeral queuing in the car park.
